payload.text: file-tree — entry operationsAdd Entry1addEntry(2  path: string,3  note?: string,4  change?: "added" | "removed" | "modified" | "renamed",5) -> props patch: { entries }DescriptionAppend a path entry (optional note and change marker) to the file tree.Paramspath · string/-separated path, no leading "./"; a trailing "/" marks an explicit directory.note · stringShort annotation rendered after the path.change · "added" | "removed" | "modified" | "renamed"Change marker rendered as a badge.Remove Entry1removeEntry(2  path: string,3) -> props patch: { entries }DescriptionRemove the entry with the given path from the file tree.Paramspath · stringExact path of the entry to remove.

payload.context: Mounted Docs application in a fresh isolated browser context; repository defaults, not private browser overrides.

payload.source: audited Interaction Surface brief; no generation started

assignment.task: Implement one interactive Interaction Surface variation by editing the copied source. Changes must be visible and match the direction.

direction.name: Operation Index and Detail
direction.intent: Use one amber textured Operations header above a compact ordered operation index and a focused detail area. Index entries retain names and query/event labels; selecting an entry reveals its complete signature, description, return value, and nested notes. Keep the index keyboard-accessible. Default to the first operation. On narrow screens put the index above details. Compare faster navigation and focus against the cost of hiding unselected details.

brief.goal: Explore the presentation of operations and their details in the approved Textured Bounded Header visual family. Use a muted orange/amber Operations identity, clear hierarchy, readable text, restrained texture, rounded boundaries, and thin cohesive separators.
brief.boundaries: Preserve operation semantics and linked signature/parameter interactions. Do not turn operations into a State Shape Field/Type ledger. Keep original source and State Shape sessions untouched. Generation requires explicit Start; Apply requires a later selected and approved design.
preserve: Keep operation order, full names when bare verbs collide, action/query/event meaning, optional markers, return values, and every parameter description.
Preserve recursive signature grammar and nested notes, bidirectional hover/focus, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, and isolation between operations.
Keep zero-parameter and no-notes operations readable. Missing descriptions stay empty. Preserve text selection and copying.
Keep the typed props, exports, Docs descriptor and wide-left integration. Support light/dark themes, narrow screens, and reduced motion.

directions.name: Bounded Operation Cards
directions.intent: Give each operation one rounded card with a restrained amber textured header containing its name, kind, and purpose. Put the signature and nested parameter notes side by side on wide screens, stacked on narrow screens. Remove repeated Description/Params bands. Compare the clarity of self-contained operation cards and their vertical rhythm.

directions.name: Continuous Operations List
directions.intent: Use one rounded component boundary and one amber textured Operations header. Keep operations in document order as continuous sections separated by a single thin rule. Place each operation purpose above its signature and align compact nested notes beside the signature. Compare scanning across many operations with less repeated card furniture; do not introduce Field/Type columns.

directions.name: Operation Index and Detail

direction.intent: Use one rounded component boundary and one amber textured Operations header. Keep operations in document order as continuous sections separated by a single thin rule. Place each operation purpose above its signature and align compact nested notes beside the signature. Compare scanning across many operations with less repeated card furniture; do not introduce Field/Type columns.

brief.goal: Explore the presentation of operations and their details in the approved Textured Bounded Header visual family. Use a muted orange/amber Operations identity, clear hierarchy, readable text, restrained texture, rounded boundaries, and thin cohesive separators.
brief.boundaries: Preserve operation semantics and linked signature/parameter interactions. Do not turn operations into a State Shape Field/Type ledger. Keep original source and State Shape sessions untouched. Generation requires explicit Start; Apply requires a later selected and approved design.
preserve: Keep operation order, full names when bare verbs collide, action/query/event meaning, optional markers, return values, and every parameter description.
Preserve recursive signature grammar and nested notes, bidirectional hover/focus, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, and isolation between operations.
Keep zero-parameter and no-notes operations readable. Missing descriptions stay empty. Preserve text selection and copying.
Keep the typed props, exports, Docs descriptor and wide-left integration. Support light/dark themes, narrow screens, and reduced motion.

directions.name: Bounded Operation Cards
directions.intent: Give each operation one rounded card with a restrained amber textured header containing its name, kind, and purpose. Put the signature and nested parameter notes side by side on wide screens, stacked on narrow screens. Remove repeated Description/Params bands. Compare the clarity of self-contained operation cards and their vertical rhythm.

directions.name: Continuous Operations List
directions.intent: Use one rounded component boundary and one amber textured Operations header. Keep operations in document order as continuous sections separated by a single thin rule. Place each operation purpose above its signature and align compact nested notes beside the signature. Compare scanning across many operations with less repeated card furniture; do not introduce Field/Type columns.

directions.name: Operation Index and Detail
directions.intent: Use one amber textured Operations header above a compact ordered operation index and a focused detail area. Index entries retain names and query/event labels; selecting an entry reveals its complete signature, description, return value, and nested notes. Keep the index keyboard-accessible. Default to the first operation. On narrow screens put the index above details. Compare faster navigation and focus against the cost of hiding unselected details.

decisions.wording: Interaction Surface should visibly belong to the same family as the approved Textured Bounded Header State Shape.
Blue identifies State Shape. Use a muted orange/amber for Interaction Surface and its Operations identity.
Keep the refined typography, spacing, restrained texture, rounded boundaries, clear hierarchy, and thin, cohesive separators.
Avoid doubled borders, heavy rules, redundant headings, and unnecessary chrome.
Preserve the component’s meaningful behavior and information. Do not force an operations component into a data-field layout.

Preserve each relevant like, dislike, and decision with its original context and scope. Distinguish explicit user decisions from your interpretations. Do not turn a State Shape-specific choice into a universal rule.
Present the brief inside Variator and leave the first generation round ready for me to explicitly press Start.
Do not Apply an Interaction Surface design yet. That requires my later selection and approval.

With this one, I think I really like the line about keeping the name of the object and its description in a section that is connected but fully separate from the paths and the example. I think that really lines things up. I don't like, though, how the column names are Field and Description, or Field Path and Description. They should be Field and Type. Those are the two columns across all of them, and that's what I like about this one.

Generally, I like this. I think the best part is that there is a standardized definition column. I don't really love the description as an extra column. I think that would be good under the field.

I kind of liked, in the previous one or in the original, the line that symbolizes that it's a child of something. I like the separation between each entity, so in each row, it makes sense. I'm just trying to find a way we can very easily and visually see that something is the child of something else.

I also don't really love the optional big flag. I want to figure out some way we could not need to represent this as optional, but represent it more compactly.

From this one, I like the side piece, but it's not perfect yet. I think the text needs to come in a little bit, and that line needs to line up with the text in the left column in the Field column. assignment.task: Propose a brief for Interaction Surface exploration. Return JSON only. Preserve every distinct micro-decision. Do not generalize a local dislike. Original user feedback is authoritative; interpretations are proposals. No batch winner is required. Never start generation.
assignment.goal: Explore the presentation of operations and their details in the approved Textured Bounded Header visual family. Use a muted orange/amber Operations identity, clear hierarchy, readable text, restrained texture, rounded boundaries, and thin cohesive separators.
assignment.boundaries: Preserve operation semantics and linked signature/parameter interactions. Do not turn operations into a State Shape Field/Type ledger. Keep original source and State Shape sessions untouched. Generation requires explicit Start; Apply requires a later selected and approved design.

designIntent.intent: Complete decision provenance for the already-written light-theme header contrast repair to Bounded Operation Cards.
designIntent.layout: No source change since the prior submission; self-contained rounded operation cards retain responsive signature and notes panes.
designIntent.spacing: No source change since the prior submission; compact bounded Operations identity and existing card rhythm remain.
designIntent.typography: No source change since the prior submission; high-contrast full-opacity header typography remains.
designIntent.colors: No source change since the prior submission; repaired light header foreground #2d1b0c and accent #6b3a0f remain against #f5eadc.
designIntent.motion: No source change since the prior submission; reduced-motion support remains intact.
designIntent.interactions: No source change since the prior submission; linked hover, focus, pinning, Escape clearing, copying, and operation isolation remain intact.
tradeoffs: None beyond those documented in the immediately preceding source submission.

designIntent.intent: A continuous Operations reference that reduces repeated card furniture while preserving complete operation semantics and linked signature-to-note behavior. One rounded boundary and one amber textured identity header frame an ordered sequence of purpose-first operation sections.
designIntent.layout: One component-level rounded container holds a connected Operations header and a document-order list. Each operation is one section separated from the next by a single thin rule. The operation heading and kind lead into its purpose, followed by a responsive signature/notes grid: signature left and compact nested notes right at medium widths, stacked on narrow screens. Zero-parameter signatures remain standalone and operations without notes omit the empty notes region.
designIntent.spacing: The header uses 16px horizontal and 14px vertical padding. Operation sections use 16px padding on narrow screens and 20px on larger screens. Compact 8–12px internal gaps keep each purpose associated with its signature while 16–20px section padding supports scanning. Nested notes indent by 12px with an 8px inset after a one-pixel guide.
designIntent.typography: Operations identity is an 11px bold uppercase monospace label with restrained tracking; the optional title and operation names use compact semibold sans text. Signatures retain deterministic monospace token styling and line treatment through CodeLines. Purpose text is 13px/20px; all parameter names, types, and descriptions are at least 12px, with descriptions at 1.45 line-height.
designIntent.colors: Component-scoped light tokens use accent #87511e, header #f5eadc/#3f2b19, rule #d8c5ad, and texture #b4793b. Dark tokens use #e0b47e, #30271e/#f3e1ca, #64503a, and #aa7841. The header texture uses two low-opacity decorative radial contours. Query and event retain distinguishable sky and violet semantics; action receives a restrained amber badge.
designIntent.motion: No decorative motion was introduced. Existing linked-panel state behavior remains, and a scoped prefers-reduced-motion rule effectively removes transition duration and animated scrolling.
designIntent.interactions: Each operation keeps its own LinkGroup, preserving isolation. Recursive parameter line spans and note keys remain bidirectionally linked for hover/focus; LinkGroup/LinkTarget retain click and Enter/Space pinning and Escape clearing. Text remains selectable and copyable. Existing data-interaction-operation, data-param-note, data-code-line (via CodeLines), and signature-token hooks are preserved.
tradeoffs: A continuous list improves multi-operation scanning but gives individual operations less self-contained visual weight than cards.
Showing the action badge adds a small amount of repeated furniture, but prevents action semantics from relying on an undocumented absence.
The signature inset adds one local boundary; it improves code legibility while remaining lighter than repeated full cards.
Notes stack beneath signatures on narrow screens, increasing vertical length in exchange for readable descriptions and touch-friendly linked targets.

designIntent.intent: Operation Index and Detail implemented in the isolated source: one amber textured Operations header, ordered keyboard-accessible index, and one focused complete operation detail.
designIntent.layout: Responsive rounded component: index at left and detail at right from medium widths, with index above detail on narrow screens.
designIntent.spacing: Compact 12–20px padding, 12px control gaps, and cohesive one-pixel separators.
designIntent.typography: Full monospace operation names and signatures; 12px or larger parameter descriptions; compact uppercase identity and semantic labels.
designIntent.colors: Component-scoped light/dark amber palette tokens with restrained decorative texture and semantic query/event badge accents.
designIntent.motion: Restrained color transitions only, disabled under reduced motion.
designIntent.interactions: First operation defaults selected. Native index buttons support click, Enter/Space, arrows, Home, and End. Selected operation uses an isolated LinkGroup preserving signature/note hover, focus, pinning, and Escape behavior.
tradeoffs: Focused detail improves navigation but hides unselected details until selected.
The side index uses some wide-screen space; it stacks to preserve narrow-screen readability.

assignment.startingPointInstruction: Recommend a retained starting design using baseVariationId, or null for the captured baseline. A current-batch winner is not required. Honor any explicit user override.

feedback.body:
Generally, I think the operations list is the best one we've had so far. I don't love it, though. I'd like the fields and related items to have the same style as the state structure, with lines between them and their children based on a tree-like structure.

For the actual function portion, I'd like it to not have the orange backlighting for the code path, but I like this general idea. I also really like the style of this background and related items. I think we want it set up so that the taper goes from left to right. Under operations or exploration operations in these headers, or in the state field structure, it's very light there, so the text is super easy to read.

On the right side, where there's no content, we can have this twisty stuff going on over there. It's moved over to the right so you can really see the coolness of that factored-in design, but it's tied like that.
I like the header on this, and I like the style of the code that defines the function surface, in the sense that it's not an orange background.
This is my favorite, except I don't like how the code section for the function surface is orange.
I don't like this one at all.

palette.instructions: Define component-scoped CSS custom properties for light and dark inside the editable renderer, including [data-operations-header] and a visible Operations label. Apply header tokens in all directions; keep texture decorative and pointer-inert. Header text must have WCAG contrast >= 4.5:1. Normal parameter descriptions >=12px. Preserve data-interaction-operation, data-param-note, data-code-line and signature token hooks. Use the captured approved State Shape renderer as read-only visual reference. Its field ledger, exact tree geometry, blue identity and JSON pane are not requirements for operations.

reference.images: Use inspect_reference_image for captured application screenshots and original feedback images.
reference.scope: Historical State Shape decisions retain their original scope; acknowledge non-applicability instead of copying field-ledger choices.

assignment.gates: Keep operation order, full names when bare verbs collide, action/query/event meaning, optional markers, return values, and every parameter description. Preserve recursive signature grammar and nested notes, bidirectional hover/focus, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, and isolation between operations. Keep zero-parameter and no-notes operations readable. Missing descriptions stay empty. Preserve text selection and copying. Keep the typed props, exports, Docs descriptor and wide-left integration. Support light/dark themes, narrow screens, and reduced motion. Keep stable data attributes. Index controls, if used, must have data-operation-select=fullOperationName. Include visible Operations identity with data-operations-header, header text contrast >=4.5:1, parameter descriptions >=12px, no page overflow, reduced-motion support.

direction.name: Tapered Tree List
direction.intent: Refine the retained Continuous Operations List most directly: use a connected amber Operations header with an exceptionally light text zone at left and restrained twist-like contours that strengthen toward empty space at right. Keep signatures on a neutral code surface. Render parameter notes as separated rows with thin, cohesive tree branches that visibly connect parents and children.

brief.goal: Explore three refinements of the Continuous Operations List within the approved Textured Bounded Header visual family. Retain the continuous, purpose-first operations presentation while testing clearer tree-like parameter relationships, neutral function-signature surfaces without orange backlighting, and a muted amber Operations header whose texture tapers from a very light, highly readable left side toward more expressive twist-like detail in unused space on the right.
brief.boundaries: Preserve operation semantics and linked signature/parameter interactions. Do not turn operations into a State Shape Field/Type ledger. Keep original source and State Shape sessions untouched. Generation requires explicit Start; Apply requires a later selected and approved design.
preserve: The Continuous Operations List as the recommended starting design because the user called it their favorite and described the operations list as the best so far, while also stating that it still needs refinement.
A connected, rounded Operations component with a readable textured amber identity header, clear hierarchy, refined typography and spacing, restrained texture, and thin cohesive separators.
A very light header area behind Operations or Exploration Operations text so that the text remains super easy to read.
A left-to-right texture taper that moves the stronger twist-like decorative treatment into unused space on the right.
A neutral function-signature/code surface without orange background or orange code-path backlighting.
Readable operation names, descriptions, kind semantics, signatures, recursive parameters, optional markers, types, and return values.
Tree-like parent-child cues and lines between parameter-related items and their children, while preserving an operations presentation rather than converting it into a State Shape Field/Type ledger.

One isolated LinkGroup per operation and bidirectional signature-to-note hover and focus linking, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, selectable and copyable text, and existing interaction hooks.
Responsive signature and notes behavior, including stacking at narrow widths, standalone zero-parameter signatures, and omission of empty notes regions.
Reduced-motion support without interpreting any local visual dislike as a global animation ban.
Absent descriptions remaining empty rather than displaying placeholder text.
The original source and all State Shape work remaining untouched.

feedback.body:
Generally, I think the operations list is the best one we've had so far. I don't love it, though. I'd like the fields and related items to have the same style as the state structure, with lines between them and their children based on a tree-like structure.

For the actual function portion, I'd like it to not have the orange backlighting for the code path, but I like this general idea. I also really like the style of this background and related items. I think we want it set up so that the taper goes from left to right. Under operations or exploration operations in these headers, or in the state field structure, it's very light there, so the text is super easy to read.

On the right side, where there's no content, we can have this twisty stuff going on over there. It's moved over to the right so you can really see the coolness of that factored-in design, but it's tied like that.
I like the header on this, and I like the style of the code that defines the function surface, in the sense that it's not an orange background.
This is my favorite, except I don't like how the code section for the function surface is orange.
I don't like this one at all.

palette.instructions: Define component-scoped CSS custom properties for light and dark inside the editable renderer, including [data-operations-header] and a visible Operations label. Apply header tokens in all directions; keep texture decorative and pointer-inert. Header text must have WCAG contrast >= 4.5:1. Normal parameter descriptions >=12px. Preserve data-interaction-operation, data-param-note, data-code-line and signature token hooks. Use the captured approved State Shape renderer as read-only visual reference. Its field ledger, exact tree geometry, blue identity and JSON pane are not requirements for operations.

reference.images: Use inspect_reference_image for captured application screenshots and original feedback images.
reference.scope: Historical State Shape decisions retain their original scope; acknowledge non-applicability instead of copying field-ledger choices.

assignment.gates: Keep operation order, full names when bare verbs collide, action/query/event meaning, optional markers, return values, and every parameter description. Preserve recursive signature grammar and nested notes, bidirectional hover/focus, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, and isolation between operations. Keep zero-parameter and no-notes operations readable. Missing descriptions stay empty. Preserve text selection and copying. Keep the typed props, exports, Docs descriptor and wide-left integration. Support light/dark themes, narrow screens, and reduced motion. Keep stable data attributes. Index controls, if used, must have data-operation-select=fullOperationName. Include visible Operations identity with data-operations-header, header text contrast >=4.5:1, parameter descriptions >=12px, no page overflow, reduced-motion support.
assignment.output: Call submit_design with design intent after writing source. Include individual inherited decision handling, layout, spacing, typography, colors, motion, interactions, builder choices, and tradeoffs. Do not just describe proposed code.

direction.name: Integrated Branch Detail
direction.intent: Keep the continuous list and neutral signature pane, but integrate tree geometry more tightly across each operation’s related parameter detail: align parent and child text, use row separators for entities, and use short terminal-style branches to establish ancestry without importing State Shape’s Field/Type columns or turning operation details into a ledger.

brief.goal: Explore three refinements of the Continuous Operations List within the approved Textured Bounded Header visual family. Retain the continuous, purpose-first operations presentation while testing clearer tree-like parameter relationships, neutral function-signature surfaces without orange backlighting, and a muted amber Operations header whose texture tapers from a very light, highly readable left side toward more expressive twist-like detail in unused space on the right.
brief.boundaries: Preserve operation semantics and linked signature/parameter interactions. Do not turn operations into a State Shape Field/Type ledger. Keep original source and State Shape sessions untouched. Generation requires explicit Start; Apply requires a later selected and approved design.
preserve: The Continuous Operations List as the recommended starting design because the user called it their favorite and described the operations list as the best so far, while also stating that it still needs refinement.
A connected, rounded Operations component with a readable textured amber identity header, clear hierarchy, refined typography and spacing, restrained texture, and thin cohesive separators.
A very light header area behind Operations or Exploration Operations text so that the text remains super easy to read.
A left-to-right texture taper that moves the stronger twist-like decorative treatment into unused space on the right.
A neutral function-signature/code surface without orange background or orange code-path backlighting.
Readable operation names, descriptions, kind semantics, signatures, recursive parameters, optional markers, types, and return values.
Tree-like parent-child cues and lines between parameter-related items and their children, while preserving an operations presentation rather than converting it into a State Shape Field/Type ledger.

One isolated LinkGroup per operation and bidirectional signature-to-note hover and focus linking, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, selectable and copyable text, and existing interaction hooks.
Responsive signature and notes behavior, including stacking at narrow widths, standalone zero-parameter signatures, and omission of empty notes regions.
Reduced-motion support without interpreting any local visual dislike as a global animation ban.
Absent descriptions remaining empty rather than displaying placeholder text.
The original source and all State Shape work remaining untouched.

directions.name: Tapered Tree List
directions.intent: Refine the retained Continuous Operations List most directly: use a connected amber Operations header with an exceptionally light text zone at left and restrained twist-like contours that strengthen toward empty space at right. Keep signatures on a neutral code surface. Render parameter notes as separated rows with thin, cohesive tree branches that visibly connect parents and children.

directions.intent: Combine the liked header and neutral code styling associated with Bounded Operation Cards with the favored scanning model of the Continuous Operations List. With this one, I think I really like the line about keeping the name of the object and its description in a section that is connected but fully separate from the paths and the example. I think that really lines things up. I don't like, though, how the column names are Field and Description, or Field Path and Description. They should be Field and Type. Those are the two columns across all of them, and that's what I like about this one.

Generally, I like this. I think the best part is that there is a standardized definition column. I don't really love the description as an extra column. I think that would be good under the field.

I kind of liked, in the previous one or in the original, the line that symbolizes that it's a child of something. I like the separation between each entity, so in each row, it makes sense. directions.name: Bounded Operation Cards
directions.intent: Give each operation one rounded card with a restrained amber textured header containing its name, kind, and purpose. Put the signature and nested parameter notes side by side on wide screens, stacked on narrow screens. Remove repeated Description/Params bands. directions.name: Continuous Operations List
directions.intent: Use one rounded component boundary and one amber textured Operations header. Keep operations in document order as continuous sections separated by a single thin rule. Place each operation purpose above its signature and align compact nested notes beside the signature. Compare scanning across many operations with less repeated card furniture; do not introduce Field/Type columns.

directions.name: Operation Index and Detail
directions.intent: Use one amber textured Operations header above a compact ordered operation index and a focused detail area. Index entries retain names and query/event labels; selecting an entry reveals its complete signature, description, return value, and nested notes. Use keyboard-accessible buttons with data-operation-select equal to the full operation name. Default to the first operation. On narrow screens put the index above details. Compare faster navigation and focus against the cost of hiding unselected details.

With this one, I think I really like the line about keeping the name of the object and its description in a section that is connected but fully separate from the paths and the example. I think that really lines things up. I don't like, though, how the column names are Field and Description, or Field Path and Description. They should be Field and Type. Those are the two columns across all of them, and that's what I like about this one.

Maybe if we had some level of wave or something in the background, it could feel better. I'm not sure. I like option 2's card shape, but for this one, I really like the texture of the background at the head of the card.

Generally, I like this. I think the best part is that there is a standardized definition column. I don't really love the description as an extra column. I think that would be good under the field.

I kind of liked, in the previous one or in the original, the line that symbolizes that it's a child of something. I like the separation between each entity, so in each row, it makes sense. I'm just trying to find a way we can very easily and visually see that something is the child of something else.

I also don't really love the optional big flag. I want to figure out some way we could not need to represent this as optional, but represent it more compactly.

From this one, I like the side piece, but it's not perfect yet. I think the text needs to come in a little bit, and that line needs to line up with the text in the left column in the Field column. I like how the children in this very clearly direct your eye to the text that they're children of. I don't like how it renders as "no description" if there's none there. I think it should be empty. This, honestly, is across the global level that I'm seeing with it.

briefs.goal: Explore three refinements of the Continuous Operations List within the approved Textured Bounded Header visual family. Retain the continuous, purpose-first operations presentation while testing clearer tree-like parameter relationships, neutral function-signature surfaces without orange backlighting, and a muted amber Operations header whose texture tapers from a very light, highly readable left side toward more expressive twist-like detail in unused space on the right.
briefs.boundaries: Preserve operation semantics and linked signature/parameter interactions. Do not turn operations into a State Shape Field/Type ledger. Keep original source and State Shape sessions untouched. Generation requires explicit Start; Apply requires a later selected and approved design.
preserve: The Continuous Operations List as the recommended starting design because the user called it their favorite and described the operations list as the best so far, while also stating that it still needs refinement.
A connected, rounded Operations component with a readable textured amber identity header, clear hierarchy, refined typography and spacing, restrained texture, and thin cohesive separators.
A very light header area behind Operations or Exploration Operations text so that the text remains super easy to read.
A left-to-right texture taper that moves the stronger twist-like decorative treatment into unused space on the right.
A neutral function-signature/code surface without orange background or orange code-path backlighting.
Readable operation names, descriptions, kind semantics, signatures, recursive parameters, optional markers, types, and return values.
Tree-like parent-child cues and lines between parameter-related items and their children, while preserving an operations presentation rather than converting it into a State Shape Field/Type ledger.

One isolated LinkGroup per operation and bidirectional signature-to-note hover and focus linking, click and Enter/Space pinning, Escape clearing, selectable and copyable text, and existing interaction hooks.
Responsive signature and notes behavior, including stacking at narrow widths, standalone zero-parameter signatures, and omission of empty notes regions.
Reduced-motion support without interpreting any local visual dislike as a global animation ban.
Absent descriptions remaining empty rather than displaying placeholder text.
The original source and all State Shape work remaining untouched.

directions.name: Tapered Tree List
directions.intent: Refine the retained Continuous Operations List most directly: use a connected amber Operations header with an exceptionally light text zone at left and restrained twist-like contours that strengthen toward empty space at right. Keep signatures on a neutral code surface. Render parameter notes as separated rows with thin, cohesive tree branches that visibly connect parents and children.

directions.name: Integrated Branch Detail
directions.intent: Keep the continuous list and neutral signature pane, but integrate tree geometry more tightly across each operation’s related parameter detail: align parent and child text, use row separators for entities, and use short terminal-style branches to establish ancestry without importing State Shape’s Field/Type columns or turning operation details into a ledger.

directions.name: Bounded List Hybrid
directions.intent: Combine the liked header and neutral code styling associated with Bounded Operation Cards with the favored scanning model of the Continuous Operations List. Use one rounded outer boundary, restrained operation separators rather than repeated heavy cards, tree-linked parameter notes, and a left-to-right tapered header texture with the expressive twist concentrated on the right.

feedback.body:
Generally, I think the operations list is the best one we've had so far. I don't love it, though. I'd like the fields and related items to have the same style as the state structure, with lines between them and their children based on a tree-like structure.

For the actual function portion, I'd like it to not have the orange backlighting for the code path, but I like this general idea. I also really like the style of this background and related items. I think we want it set up so that the taper goes from left to right. Under operations or exploration operations in these headers, or in the state field structure, it's very light there, so the text is super easy to read.

On the right side, where there's no content, we can have this twisty stuff going on over there. It's moved over to the right so you can really see the coolness of that factored-in design, but it's tied like that.
